summary: This manuscript addresses the fundamental bottlenecks in extracting spectral gaps and continuum threshold exponents from imaginary-time evolution (ITE), introducing an exact cumulant-covariance identity (Thm 2.1), shift-invariant cumulant estimators achieving exact O(tau^-2) bias reduction (Thm 2.3), spectral-edge trichotomy (Thm 3.1), exact-Q Stieltjes-Hankel upper certificates (Thm 4.1), and Le Cam minimax resolution limits (Thm 5.1), backed by 16 Lean 4 theorems.
weaknesses: Third-cumulant estimation increases sensitivity to additive measurement noise at low SNR (sigma >= 10^-6).
Certifying lower bounds without explicit physical structures remains impossible from finite-tau moments alone.
